stories.title: S3 Capital Supplies $20M for Boutique Miami Beach Condo
stories.excerpt: Trinity Southern has closed on the purchase of a development site and nabbed a $19.5 million construction loan for a boutique condo development on the waterfront in Miami Beach, property records show. S3 Capital provided the financing for the eight-story development, called Twenty Nine Indian Creek, at 2901 Indian Creek Drive in the Mid-Beach neighborhood, near the Miami Beach Edition hotel. In tandem with the financing, the New York-based developer broke ground and purchased the 15,000-square-foot site for $8 million from another New York-based firm, JMH Development, which had initially proposed the condo development. Twenty Nine Indian Creek will house 16 units, totaling 24,842 square feet of sellable space, and a parking garage, according to a filing to Miami-Dade County. So far, 10 units have sold, Dana Lozito, who leads Trinity Southern, told Commercial Observer. Luxury condo developments in Miami Beach, and South Florida more broadly, remain attractive to lenders. Just this week, a Terra-led partnership has secured a $507 million construction loan for a condo tower in South Beach. In an unusual move, the financing from Tyko Capital came even before the sponsors had launched sales. Typically, developments need to hit certain sales benchmarks before securing funding. Last year, Mast Capital and Starwood Capital Group landed $390 million in construction debt for a OMA-designed project in Mid-Beach. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: S3 Capital closed $19.5M construction loan for Trinity Southern's 16-unit luxury condo in Miami Beach.
Twenty Nine Indian Creek at 2901 Indian Creek Drive; 10 of 16 units presold before ground break.
Site acquired for $8M from JMH Development; eight-story waterfront development near Miami Beach Edition.
stories.summary: Trinity Southern acquired a 15,000-square-foot Miami Beach waterfront site for $8 million and secured $19.5 million in construction financing from S3 Capital for Twenty Nine Indian Creek, an eight-story boutique condo with 16 units. The property, located in the Mid-Beach neighborhood near Miami Beach Edition, has already presold 10 units. Luxury condo financing in South Florida remains active and attractive to lenders.
stories.impact: Miami Beach condo strength signals continued affluent in-migration and wealth concentration in South Florida; while not multifamily rental, this capital activity and presale velocity in luxury demonstrates robust demand for experiential urban living near hotels and mixed-use, which can inform adjacent rental demand patterns and land values in South Florida submarkets.

stories.title: Nuveen Acquires 113K-SF Aurora Retail Center
stories.excerpt: Nuveen Real Estate has acquired Highpoint Marketplace, a 113,833-square-foot retail center in Aurora, Colo. Commercial Search reports that Gerrity Group sold the asset for $36.3 million or roughly $319 per square foot. Gerrity Group paid $24 million for the Safeway-anchored center in 2018. Located at 18730 E. Hampden Ave., the three-building property opened in 2001 on nearly 15 acres just east of South Tower Road. Highpoint Marketplace in a residential area within 9 miles of the city center and 15 miles southeast of downtown Denver. The retail center last underwent renovations in 2007. Anchored by a 55,580-square-foot Safeway, the property also has fitness, beauty, health and dining tenants such as Wendy’s on its roster. CM Commercial Partners oversees leasing. Gerrity owns and operates 19 properties throughout the western United States, with a focus on grocery-anchored shopping centers. The post Nuveen Acquires 113K-SF Aurora Retail Center appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Nuveen acquired Highpoint Marketplace, Aurora, Colo., 113,833 SF for $36.3M ($319/SF) from Gerrity Group.
Safeway-anchored center on 15 acres; Gerrity paid $24M in 2018; last renovated 2007.
Aurora location 9 miles east of city center, 15 miles southeast of downtown Denver.
stories.summary: Nuveen Real Estate purchased Highpoint Marketplace, a 113,833-square-foot Safeway-anchored retail center in Aurora, Colorado, for $36.3 million ($319/SF). Gerrity Group, which bought the asset in 2018 for $24 million, sold it after a 51-percent gain over six years. The three-building property occupies 15 acres in a residential area and was last renovated in 2007.
stories.impact: Little direct relevance to multifamily development; retail capital flows do not signal apartment demand or supply conditions in Aurora or metro Denver.

stories.title: Interstate Equities Pays $84M for Hercules Multifamily
stories.excerpt: JLL Capital Markets arranged the $83.5-million sale and $54.275-million financing of The Dylan, a 232-unit apartment community in Hercules. JLL represented the seller, Hercules Development Partners, in the sale to Interstate Equities Corporation and arranged a five-year acquisition loan through Freddie Mac. Senior managing directors Ryan Wagner, Brandon Geraldo and Matt Kroger and director Fatai Alashe of JLL’s Capital Markets Investment Sales and Advisory team represented the seller. Executive managing director Charles Halladay and director Matt Cimino led the Capital Markets Debt Advisory team representing the borrower. Completed in 2022, The Dylan is located along San Pablo Bay at 2200 John Muir Pkwy. “The East Bay continues to attract significant investor attention due to its relative affordability compared to core Bay Area markets, robust income growth projections and limited new supply,” said Wagner. “Hercules, with its unique waterfront position and excellent regional connectivity, has emerged as a standout performer.” The post Interstate Equities Pays $84M for Hercules Multifamily appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Interstate Equities acquired The Dylan, Hercules, CA, 232 units for $83.5M; Freddie Mac financed $54.3M.
Completed 2022 at 2200 John Muir Pkwy along San Pablo Bay; five-year acquisition loan term.
East Bay multifamily attracting investors due to affordability vs. core Bay Area and limited new supply.
stories.summary: Interstate Equities purchased The Dylan, a 232-unit apartment community completed in 2022 in Hercules, California, for $83.5 million with a $54.3 million Freddie Mac acquisition loan. The waterfront East Bay property is benefiting from investor appetite driven by relative affordability compared to core San Francisco Bay Area and a constrained supply pipeline. JLL Capital Markets arranged the sale and financing.
stories.impact: Hercules submarket (East Bay) is crystallizing as a flight-to-value destination for institutional buyers seeking Bay Area exposure without prime SF/Oakland pricing; this signals opportunity for TCR to acquire or develop mid-market multifamily in East Bay submarkets ahead of further supply constraints and rent escalation as East Bay becomes the default affordable option for Bay Area job growth.

stories.title: ORIX Buys 322-Unit Austin Apartment Community
stories.excerpt: ORIX Corp. USA has purchased Strata, a 322-unit luxury asset in Austin, Texas, from Maverick Development Group. In addition, Multi-Housing New reports Franklin BSP Realty Trust issued a $42 million acquisition loan set to mature in 2031. Strata is part of a six-phase project set to include more than 2,000 units. ORIX’s new community comprises 12 buildings encompassing studio, one- and two-bedroom layouts that average 875 square feet. Amenities include a business lounge with private work pods, as well as a gym, swimming pool and community room, among other features. Located at 8340 Bluff Springs Road, Strata is some 10 miles southwest of downtown Austin. The property is also less than 1 mile from Interstate 35. Established in 1981, ORIX manages proprietary and investor capital across a wide range of alternative asset classes on the ORIX USA platform and through subsidiaries NXT Capital, Hilco Global, Boston Financial and Lument. The post ORIX Buys 322-Unit Austin Apartment Community appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: ORIX acquired Strata, Austin, TX, 322 units from Maverick Development; Franklin BSP issued $42M loan (matures 2031).
Located 10 miles southwest downtown at 8340 Bluff Springs Rd; part of six-phase project totaling 2,000+ units.
Luxury asset with studio/1BR/2BR averaging 875 SF; amenities include business lounge, gym, pool.
stories.summary: ORIX Corp. USA purchased Strata, a 322-unit luxury apartment community in Austin, Texas, from Maverick Development Group. Franklin BSP Realty Trust financed the acquisition with a $42 million loan maturing in 2031. The property, located 10 miles southwest of downtown and less than 1 mile from Interstate 35, is part of a larger six-phase project expected to deliver over 2,000 units.
stories.impact: Austin's continued attractiveness to institutional capital on a multi-thousand-unit pipeline indicates sustained demand momentum and developer confidence in market absorption; TCR should monitor supply timing and phase-out across the six-phase project to identify windows for selective infill development or acquisition of remaining parcels before downstream saturation pressures emerge in southwest Austin corridor.

stories.title: Lincoln Moving Ahead on Uptown Mixed-Use Project
stories.excerpt: Lincoln Property Co.⁠ expects to break ground on an office tower of more than 500,000 square feet later this year or in early 2028. To be called 28Hundred Fairmount, it will anchor an even wider development the company is calling The Springs District, totaling 1.4 million square feet on a 4-acre site at 2500 Cedar Springs Road. The project will also have an as-yet-unnamed 234-unit apartment tower and 200-key hotel. The Dallas Business Journal reports that all are expected to be complete by 2030. Lincoln is developing the entire district. Suffolk Construction has been brought on board as general contractor. The planned tower is less than a half-mile from Uptown’s newest and tallest tower, 23Springs. The post Lincoln Moving Ahead on Uptown Mixed-Use Project appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Lincoln Property Co. breaking ground late 2027/early 2028 on 500K+ SF office tower at 2500 Cedar Springs Rd, Dallas.
The Springs District mixed-use: 28Hundred Fairmount office, 234-unit apartment tower, 200-key hotel; 1.4M SF total.
All components expected complete by 2030; Suffolk Construction as GC; less than 0.5 miles from 23Springs.
stories.summary: Lincoln Property Company is advancing The Springs District, a 1.4-million-square-foot mixed-use development on a 4-acre Uptown Dallas site that will include a 500,000-square-foot office tower (28Hundred Fairmount), a 234-unit apartment tower, and a 200-key hotel. Suffolk Construction is the general contractor, with groundbreaking planned for late 2027 or early 2028 and delivery by 2030. The project sits within a half-mile of the newly completed 23Springs tower.
stories.impact: Lincoln's 234-unit residential component in Uptown Dallas signals developer confidence in sustained demand density and pricing power in core Uptown; clustering with 23Springs creates a sub-market momentum play. For TCR: this Uptown activation reinforces the corridor as a high-barrier-to-entry employment and lifestyle hub; any remaining infill sites nearby should be prioritized before entitlements and land cost rise further, and consider whether build-to-suit or value-add acquisition opportunities exist in adjacent secondary Uptown blocks.

stories.title: Sycamore-Led Team Converting Nursing Home to 75 Supportive Units
stories.excerpt: Hunt Capital Partners, Sycamore Development, and ASD – A Home for Life announced the financial closing of The Meadow, a $33 million rehabilitation development at 8130 Meadow Road in Dallas. The project, led by Sycamore Development and co-developed by ASD, will convert a former nursing home facility constructed in 2016 into 75 new homes with Permanent Supportive Housing (PSH). Through adaptive reuse, the development will preserve its existing structure while providing housing for families and individuals facing significant barriers to securing a stable home. Residents will include individuals and families impacted by homelessness, people living with HIV, veterans with disabilities, individuals affected by substance use, and those protected under the Violence Against Women Act (VAWA). Financing for the project includes a $21 million construction loan from Huntington National Bank and a $13.5 million soft loan from the City of Dallas. Hunt Capital Partners syndicated $20 million in Federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credits through its multi-investor fund, Hunt Capital Partners Tax Credit Fund 52. The post Sycamore-Led Team Converting Nursing Home to 75 Supportive Units appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Sycamore Development and ASD converting former 2016 nursing home to 75 Permanent Supportive Housing units in Dallas.
The Meadow at 8130 Meadow Road; $33M total development cost; $21M construction loan from Huntington.
Financing includes $20M Low-Income Housing Tax Credits (Hunt Capital Tax Credit Fund 52) and $13.5M City soft loan.
stories.summary: Sycamore Development and ASD closed The Meadow, a $33 million adaptive reuse conversion of a former 2016 nursing home into 75 Permanent Supportive Housing units in Dallas. Hunt Capital Partners syndicated $20 million in Federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credits, Huntington National Bank provided a $21 million construction loan, and the City of Dallas contributed a $13.5 million soft loan. The project will house individuals and families experiencing homelessness, veterans, and those with disabilities.
stories.impact: PSH development activity in Dallas reflects city-level investment in supportive housing and developer confidence in LIHTC syndication markets; while targeting different demographics than standard multifamily, adaptive reuse of healthcare real estate is a secondary market signal—nursing home-to-housing conversions may accelerate post-COVID amid oversupply in senior care real estate, creating acquisition opportunities for developers with tax-credit expertise or social-housing positioning.

stories.title: Manhattan’s Office Sector Has Become the Corporate World’s Surest Bet
stories.excerpt: With every new Manhattan office report of late, the good news flows like lava. Leasing volume was up 2.3 percent in the third quarter from the same time last year. Vacancy was at 12.6 percent — the lowest level since before 2020 — down from 13.1 percent at the end of the second quarter and from 14.7 percent last year at this time. Direct asking rent was up to $84.56 per square foot, with rents over $300 no longer a rarity and $400 per square foot in the market’s sights. And, these metrics were “broad-based across major industries,” according to JLL, indicating that the current success of the office sector is not reliant on any one segment of the market. The current health of Manhattan’s office leasing can be seen not just in the big picture numbers, but also in the size and duration of some of its biggest office deals and leases this year. While Commercial Observer’s Office Deal of the Year, the 2 million-square-foot, 55-story deal for American Express to establish its new global headquarters at 2 World Trade Center, is not a lease, as American Express will solely own the building, it is a strong indicator of the company’s faith in the future of New York as the business world’s central hub as well as a notable addition to the city’s office landscape. Beyond that, this year has seen law firm Simpson Thacher & Bartlett sign for 916,000 square feet over 26 of the 29 stories at Extell Development’s 570 Fifth Avenue, Bank of America add 600,000 square feet to its existing 1.8 million square feet at One Bryant Park over a 20-year term, and Anthropic ink a full-building deal for 330 Hudson Street. The only seemingly potential dark cloud on the horizon for Manhattan office leasing is a lack of supply. It has roughly 7.9 million square feet currently under construction and expected to come online between 2028 and 2032, but much of that space is already pre-leased. bullets: Manhattan office leasing up 2.3% YoY in Q3 2026; vacancy 12.6%, lowest since pre-2020; rents up to $84.56/SF.

Direct asking rent reached $84.56 per square foot, with significant blocks trading above $300/SF and $400/SF anticipated. stories.impact: Manhattan office recovery signals strong corporate anchoring and high-income job growth in NYC; this supports robust multifamily demand for talent attraction and retention. For TCR: NYC's office momentum underscores the necessity of integrated development strategy in Manhattan and outer boroughs—acquire multifamily sites near office clusters (Midtown, FiDi, Hudson Yards) to capture white-collar rental demand influx; anticipate secondary wave of demand in Queens and Brooklyn as office tenants expand footprint and workforce dispersal accelerates.

stories.title: Law Firm Seward & Kissel Signs 171K-SF Renewal at One Battery Park Plaza
stories.excerpt: Seward & Kissel is staying put in the Financial District. The financial services law firm has renewed its 171,112-square-foot office lease for a term of 11 years with Rudin Management and Allianz Real Estate at One Battery Park Plaza, according to CBRE’s office report for the third quarter of 2026. The asking rent was not disclosed, but the average asking rent for office space in Lower Manhattan was $62.40 per square foot in the third quarter, the report noted. Kevin Daly and Craig Panzirer represented Rudin in-house while CBRE’s Lewis Miller, Andrew Sussman, Cara Chayet and Scott Sloves negotiated on behalf of Seward & Kissel. “Their renewal extends a remarkable year of leasing at the building and across the portfolio, adding to the momentum of the Downtown market,” Michael Rudin, co-CEO of Rudin, said in a statement. CBRE did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Seward & Kissel has been in the building since 2011 and occupies the 19th through 24th floors. One Battery Park Plaza, also known as 24 State Street, is a 35-story tower between Bridge and Pearl streets that overlooks Battery Park. Other tenants in the building include financial advisory firm and Northwestern Mutual affiliate SFA Agency, which expanded to ​​14,071 square feet in the 35-story building in June, as well as the New York City Independent Budget Office, a government oversight group, which took 18,765 square feet in February. Nationwide Mutual Insurance also took 38,107 square feet, and the International Refugee Assistance Project signed a deal for 19,407 square feet in 2022. Rudin built the 870,000-square-foot office building in 1971, with Allianz taking a stake in ownership in 2016. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Seward & Kissel renewed 171,112-SF office lease at One Battery Park Plaza, Financial District; 11-year term.
Tenant occupies floors 19–24; average asking rent Lower Manhattan $62.40/SF Q3 2026.
Firm has been tenant since 2011; renewal signals continued Downtown leasing momentum and tenant retention.
stories.summary: Law firm Seward & Kissel renewed its 171,112-square-foot office lease at One Battery Park Plaza in Manhattan's Financial District for an 11-year term, retaining occupancy of the 19th through 24th floors. The firm has been a tenant since 2011. The renewal occurs in an environment where average asking rent in Lower Manhattan reached $62.40 per square foot in Q3 2026.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact to multifamily; primarily an office leasing signal. However, Seward & Kissel's long-term commitment and renewal in FiDi reinforces downtown Manhattan as a stable employment anchor, supporting sustained multifamily demand in lower Manhattan and nearby outer-borough residential markets (DUMBO, Williamsburg, Long Island City).

stories.title: Law Firm Morgan & Morgan Signs 71K-SF Lease at One Seaport Plaza
stories.excerpt: Personal injury law firm Morgan & Morgan has signed a 70,602-square-foot lease at 199 Water Street, also known as One Seaport Plaza, according to third-quarter Manhattan office reports from Colliers and CBRE. Morgan & Morgan will move from a sublease to a long-term direct lease as part of the new deal, according to a source. The law firm moved into the building as a subtenant during the third quarter of 2023, relocating from Midtown and originally taking 34,792 square feet, according to a report issued at the time from the Downtown Alliance. This new lease gives the law firm a more permanent home at Jack Resnick & Sons’ One Seaport Plaza and expands its office footprint. Cushman & Wakefield brokered the deal for both the tenant and the landlord. C&W and Morgan & Morgan did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s requests for comment. The length of the lease was unclear, but asking rents at the building range between $65 and $70 per square foot, according to a source. Built in 1984 on Water Street between John and Fulton streets, One Seaport Plaza spans over 1 million square feet, offering amenities that include a cafe and lounge area. Other tenants in the building include fintech firm VCT Holdings, insurance firm Seneca and law firm Foster Garvey. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Morgan & Morgan signed 70,602-SF lease at One Seaport Plaza (199 Water Street), upgrading from sublet.
Law firm relocated from Midtown Q3 2023 as subtenant (34,792 SF); now taking direct lease and expanding footprint.
Asking rents $65–$70/SF; Seaport location (Lower Manhattan waterfront) emerging as secondary office hub.
stories.summary: Personal injury law firm Morgan & Morgan signed a long-term direct lease for 70,602 square feet at One Seaport Plaza (199 Water Street) in Manhattan's Financial District, expanding from its 34,792-square-foot sublet that began in Q3 2023. The firm originally relocated from Midtown to the Seaport location. Asking rents at the building range between $65 and $70 per square foot.
stories.impact: Morgan & Morgan's expansion and transition from sublease to direct lease signals sustained Seaport/Lower Manhattan office leasing and tenant confidence; the shift from Midtown indicates secondary office markets are absorbing high-value tenants. For TCR: Seaport's emerging status as a secondary office anchor should drive residential multifamily analysis in adjacent Tribeca, SoHo, and DUMBO submarkets—expect continued white-collar in-migration and rent pressure in walkable, waterfront-proximate rental housing.

stories.title: City National Bank of Florida Sells Former HQ in Coral Gables After Moving Out
stories.excerpt: After moving across the street earlier this year, City National Bank of Florida has sold its former headquarters in Coral Gables, Fla., for $39 million, property records show. Nonprofit hospital operator Baptist Health South Florida purchased the four-story office building at 2855 South Le Jeune Road, two blocks west of Ponce Circle Park, between Sevilla and Palermo avenues. The 121,418-square-foot building was built in 2007 on a 0.7-acre site. Last year, the bank signed a 144,878-square-foot lease to relocate at 2701 South Le Jeune Road to bring its workforce, which is based in Miami-Dade County, under one roof. Earlier this year, the tenant moved into the 15-story property, which is owned by Zara’s billionaire founder Amancio Ortega. At its former headquarters, City National Bank of Florida first owned the ground-floor space before buying the top-floor office condos for $10 million in 2017, the South Florida Business Journal reported. It’s unclear how Baptist Health South Florida, one of the largest health networks in the region, plans to use the building. It operates a corporate office at 6855 Red Road, near South Miami. Coral Gables, a wealthy suburb next to Miami, has seen an uptick in office sales in recent months. In July, insurance giant PGIM sold a 717,805-square-foot asset for nearly $100 million. In January, Deutsche Bank offloaded 3-acre property for nearly $120 million. A spokesperson for City National Bank of Florida declined to comment. A representative for Baptist Health South Florida did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: City National Bank of Florida sold former HQ at 2855 South Le Jeune Road, Coral Gables, for $39M to Baptist Health.
121,418-SF office building (built 2007, 0.7 acres); bank relocated across street to 2701 South Le Jeune Rd.
Bank relocated to 144,878-SF in Amancio Ortega-owned 15-story property to consolidate Miami-Dade workforce.
stories.summary: City National Bank of Florida sold its former headquarters, a 121,418-square-foot office building built in 2007 at 2855 South Le Jeune Road in Coral Gables, for $39 million to nonprofit hospital operator Baptist Health South Florida. The bank relocated across the street to a 144,878-square-foot lease at 2701 South Le Jeune Road, a 15-story property owned by Amancio Ortega, to consolidate its Miami-Dade workforce.
stories.impact: Baptist Health's acquisition of office real estate signals healthcare system expansion and real-estate consolidation in Coral Gables, but does not directly impact multifamily demand. The broader dynamic—corporate HQ relocation within Miami-Dade—suggests continued institutional confidence in South Florida and potential for workplace-adjacent multifamily demand if Baptist Health expands headcount; however, the 2007-built office structure may become a conversion target if Coral Gables zoning/economics allow adaptive reuse to multifamily, creating a secondary development pipeline opportunity.
